content:
A former Ohio music pastor who once appeared on "American Idol" was convicted on Tuesday of murdering his wife, whom he killed during an extramarital affair.

Prosecutors said Caleb Flynn, 40, shot and killed his 37-year-old wife Ashley Flynn, a schoolteacher and volleyball coach, in February and staged a home invasion robbery.

Flynn claimed his wife was killed by intruders, and will receive his sentence on Monday, facing a maximum penalty of life in prison without parole.

As the judge read the guilty verdicts for murder, felonious assault, and tampering with evidence, Flynn closed his eyes, shook his head to the side, and struggled to maintain his composure. After the judge dismissed the jury, he broke down in tears. His defense attorney described the verdict as "disappointing" and said an appeal was expected.

Flynn appeared on "American Idol" in 2013, telling television viewers how his wife encouraged him to pursue his dream of competing on the singing show. He sang before judges Mariah Carey, Randy Jackson, and Nicki Minaj, but ultimately failed to advance to the Hollywood round.

In closing arguments on Tuesday, prosecutors told the jury that Flynn wanted out of his marriage and shot his wife at their home in Tipp City, a town north of Dayton. Flynn and their two daughters were both home when police arrived.

Miami County Assistant Prosecutor Matthew Joseph said that the night before the fatal shooting, Flynn texted his mistress: "I choose you. I'm free. The action starts tomorrow."

Prosecutors noted that Flynn did not want to lose his two daughters, his high-paying position at his wife's family business, or his standing in the church.

Joseph said: "He wanted to keep his mistress and wanted both daughters for himself."

Although prosecutors did not find the murder weapon used to kill Ashley Flynn, they noted the scene was covered in his fingerprints and DNA. Prosecutors also said his electronic devices showed he had been moving around the house at the time, despite having told investigators he was sleeping when his wife was shot.

During the trial, a woman who claimed to have had an affair with Flynn took the stand and testified that Flynn had told her he hated his wife and had even entertained thoughts of killing her.

Flynn's defense attorney told the jury on Tuesday that investigators had never found any evidence proving Flynn fired a gun that day.

Defense attorney Patrick Mulligan said: "Being unfaithful is not the same as murder. The question is not 'Was he a good husband?'"

Mulligan also said Flynn's texts to his mistress complaining about his wife were simply meant to please her.

Alleigha Botner testified that she met Flynn in 2022, when she was 20 and interning at his church, and that the affair lasted more than a year. In court, Botner read portions of text messages between her and Flynn.

About six months before the killing, Flynn wrote: "Last night I was crying until 4 a.m., really thinking about how to kill her without going to prison myself."
